methods.label: Find the sides using 30° right triangles
methods.explanation:
Trisecting the rectangle’s right angle gives three angles of \(30^\circ\). The rays occur in the order \(CB,CE,CF,CD\), so \(\angle BCE=\angle DCF=30^\circ\). This gives two special right triangles that determine the rectangle’s sides in succession.

In a right triangle with a \(30^\circ\) angle, if the opposite leg has length \(t>0\), the hypotenuse has length \(2t\). By the Pythagorean theorem, the other leg has length
\[
\sqrt{(2t)^2-t^2}=t\sqrt3.
\]
Apply this to right triangle \(BCE\). Since \(BE=6\) is opposite its \(30^\circ\) angle,
\[
BC=6\sqrt3.
\]
Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so \(AD=6\sqrt3\). Since \(AF=2\) and \(F\) lies on \(AD\),
\[
DF=6\sqrt3-2.
\]
In right triangle \(DCF\), the leg \(DF\) is opposite \(30^\circ\). Therefore
\[
DC=\sqrt3\,DF=18-2\sqrt3.
\]
Both dimensions are positive. Thus the rectangle’s area is
\[
BC\cdot DC
=6\sqrt3(18-2\sqrt3)
=108\sqrt3-36
\approx151.1.
\]
The closest listed value is \(150\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
